**Where we are ahead:** the only LMS/HSS in pure Zig with no C dependency, next to `xmss`
in the same collection; verification is allocation-free and total (every length and
typecode checked before it indexes; a fuzz harness with a real-signature corpus);
byte-exact against the RFC's Appendix F for verification, key regeneration and signature
reproduction; the `SigningKey` handle writes the next position before any signature byte
exists and has a lock and a copy guard; all HSS levels 1..8 with any parameter mix.
**Where we are behind:** SHA-256/256 sets only (no SHA-256/192, no SHAKE256 sets — SP
800-208 and the later additional-parameter-sets RFC); single-threaded key generation
(H20 takes hours, H25 days); no serialisation of the secret key beyond `(SEED, I,
levels, position)`, which is deliberate but means every restart rebuilds the trees; no
RFC vector for W1 and W2; never run against a foreign implementation as a black-box
oracle; no mutation run and no stack-residue test (→ Backlog).

## Design & invariants

**Spec:** RFC 8554, sections 3.3 (formats), 4 (LM-OTS), 5 (LMS), 6 (HSS), Appendix A
(pseudorandom key generation), B (`p`, `ls` from `n`, `w`), C (iterative public-key
computation).

- **Layout.** `src/params.zig` (typecodes and Table 1/2 constants; `p` and `ls` are
  checked against Appendix B's formulas in a test), `src/core.zig` (hash layouts,
  LM-OTS, wire formats, every verification path), `src/sign.zig` (`Tree`, `LmsSecretKey`,
  HSS `SecretKey`, `SigningKey`), `src/root.zig` (meta, re-exports, fuzz).
- **Hash layouts** are the RFC's byte-for-byte: chain step `H(I || u32(q) || u16(i) ||
  u8(j) || x)`, message hash `H(I || u32(q) || u16(0x8181) || C || msg)`, public-key
  hash with `D_PBLC = 0x8080`, leaf `D_LEAF = 0x8282`, interior `D_INTR = 0x8383`.
  `Cksm` is Algorithm 2 with the shift `ls`, `coef` is §3.1.3's formula; their edge
  values (all-zero and all-one hashes for every `w`) are asserted.
- **Verification** is Algorithms 4a/4b/6/6a and §6.3, with the RFC's checks in a
  fail-closed order: the expected length follows from the *key's* parameter sets, so
  `sig.len` is compared first; then the two typecodes inside the signature, then
  `q < 2^h`; only then is anything indexed. `HssPublicKey.verify` takes `L` from the key
  and demands `Nspk + 1 == L` (with `L` in 1..8); each non-final signature's length is
  known from the key it is checked under, so no self-describing length is ever trusted.
  The embedded next-level public key is parsed (typecodes and length) before it becomes
  the next key. `verify` is public-data-only: plain `std.mem.eql` on the root.
- **Key derivation (Appendix A).** `x_q[i] = H(I || u32(q) || u16(i) || 0xff || SEED)`,
  reproduced by the RFC's own Test Case 2 (below). The private key of one tree is
  `(SEED, I)` plus the next leaf; nothing else is secret.
- **The randomizer `C`.** RFC 8554 wants `C` uniformly random or "another unpredictable
  process" (§7.1). There is no RNG in the module, so `C = H(I || u32(q) || u16(0xffff) ||
  0xff || SEED)`: `i = 0xffff` is unreachable by a chain index (`i <= 264`), so the hash
  input is distinct from every other use of `H`. It is a function of the secret and the
  leaf, so it is unpredictable to an attacker and, because each leaf signs once,
  never repeated across messages. `Tree.signWithRandomizer` exists so the KATs can feed
  the RFC's `C`.
- **Tree storage and cost.** A `Tree` caches every public node at height `>= c`, where
  `c = max(0, h - 15)`: at most `2^16 - 1` nodes (2 MiB). The `c` lowest levels of the
  authentication path are rebuilt per signature from sibling subtrees (`2^c - 1`
  leaves: 31 for H20, 1 023 for H25). `Tree.initCached` takes `c` explicitly; a test
  builds one H5 tree with `c` = 0, 2, 3, 5 and compares every root and a spread of
  signatures byte for byte, because H20/H25 (the only sets with `c > 0` by default) are
  not built in tests. Key generation is `2^h` LM-OTS public keys — `p (2^w - 1) + p`
  hashes each — and is not parallel.
- **HSS state.** The private key is `(SEED, I_0, level list, Position)`, `Position`
  being the leaf index used at every level for the *next* signature. The tree at level
  `i >= 1` for a position is a pure function of `SEED` and the parents' leaf path
  (`deriveChild`: two domain-tagged SHA-256 hashes over `path || SEED`), regenerated when
  the position leaves it and certified by its parent at leaf `q_{i-1}`. Deterministic
  derivation plus deterministic `C` means re-deriving a tree after a restart re-signs the
  same message at the same leaf and yields identical bytes — no second message ever
  meets a leaf except at the bottom, which is what the position counts. RFC §6 requires
  each LMS key pair to be "generated independently"; here they are pseudorandom and
  independent under SHA-256 (Appendix A permits a pseudorandom method), not
  freshly random. **No level's parameter sets change over the key's life** (§6, MUST NOT).
  `SecretKey.init` builds only the top tree (§6.1 allows delaying the rest); the first
  `sign` builds the others, and crossing a lower-tree boundary costs `O(2^h)` hashing for
  that one signature.
- **What is not stored or exposed:** there is no serialisation of the private key. A
  restart is `SecretKey.init(levels, SEED, I_0, saved_position)`.

## Statefulness — the key hazard

Two signatures from one leaf reveal enough chain values to forge a third message; the
scheme's security argument collapses per leaf, not per signature (RFC 8554 §5.4.1, §9.2).

- `sign` reads the position, builds any missing tree (may fail with `OutOfMemory`, and a
  failure there burns nothing), calls the persistence hook if one is set, **advances the
  position**, and only then produces the signature over the message. It returns
  `error.KeyExhausted` when the last leaf of the last tree has been used and never signs
  again. `OutputTooSmall` and hook failures are checked before the advance.
- A bare `SecretKey` / `LmsSecretKey` is **not thread-safe** and has no copy guard: two
  racing `sign` calls can read the same position and sign two messages at one leaf; a
  copied struct is two keys at the same position. `SigningKey` is the handle that is safe
  to share: one spin lock over the whole sequence, a `home` pointer that makes a copy
  refuse (`KeyHandleCopied`), and the `Persist` hook receiving the position that must
  already be durable before the signature at the previous one is released.
- What the module cannot do for you: put that position on stable storage (the hook is
  the seam), never restore an older copy, partition leaves between signers. **CNSA 2.0
  requires signature generation and state management inside validated hardware, and
  excludes HSS with `L > 1` (`"the multitree algorithms HSS and XMSSMT are not allowed"`,
  CNSA 2.0 FAQ v2.1, as quoted in `modules/xmss/SPEC.md`)** — so for a CNSA-governed signer
  use `L = 1` and an HSM; this software is fit for the verifier, and for signers whose
  policy is SP 800-208 without CNSA's hardware rule. Treat `sign` here as correct but
  not compliant.

## Validation — what is byte-exact and what is round-trip

RFC 8554 Appendix F, transcribed by script from the RFC text into `src/kat_vectors.zig`
(each string is the in-order concatenation of the RFC's field values; sizes are asserted):

1. **Test Case 1** (HSS L = 2, H5 / W8 at both levels): the HSS signature verifies; every
   single bit of the public key (480) and of the message (1 296) is rejected; every bit
   of the first and last 64 signature bytes and one rotating bit of every other byte
   are rejected; the LMS layer verifies on its own; truncation and extension are rejected.
   The RFC gives no private key for it.
2. **Test Case 2** (HSS L = 2, H10 / W4 over H5 / W8, generated with Appendix A): the HSS
   signature verifies; the top public key regenerates from the RFC's SEED and I (1 024
   leaves of W4); the second-level public key (inside the signature) regenerates; and
   **both LMS signatures are reproduced byte for byte** (`q`, LM-OTS signature, tree
   type, all authentication-path nodes) when the RFC's own randomizer `C` is supplied.
   That pins Appendix A, `Cksm`/`coef` at W4 and W8, the chain layout, the leaf and
   interior hashes and the path order against an external answer.
3. **LM-OTS W1 and W2 have no RFC vector.** They share every code path with W4/W8 (only
   `w`, `p`, `ls` differ, and those are checked against Appendix B's formulas); they are
   covered by round trips, the recursive-definition test and the fuzz harness, not by an
   external answer. **H15/H20/H25 are not built in the tests** (cost); their `Tree`
   differs from H5/H10 in constants and the cache height only.

Round trips and the stateful discipline (`src/unit_test.zig`): every `w` at H5, H10 at
W2; HSS `L = 1..8`; mixed parameter sets; the position strictly increasing across a
lower-tree boundary; a key exhausted after exactly `32 x 32` signatures (HSS) and 32 (LMS);
a key restored at a `Position` signs the same bytes as the walked one; the persistence
hook's order and a failed write burning nothing; the copy guard; seed wiping; every
wrong length, typecode, `q >= 2^h`, `Nspk` and `L` a typed error or `false`; the tree root
and every cached node against §5.3's recursive definition.

## Threat notes

- **verify** takes attacker-controlled bytes and is allocation-free; the fuzz harness
  (`fuzz: verify never panics …`, plus a pinned corpus of a real signature and one-bit
  mutants) drives HSS, LMS and a forced-prefix LMS form.
- **No constant-time claim**, and none is needed for the algorithm's shape: every loop
  bound in signing depends on the message digest `Q` (public: it is recomputable from
  the signature) and on parameters, never on the secret; the secret enters only as hash
  input. Timing of the hash itself is `std.crypto`'s.
- **Secret handling:** SEED, the derived `x` values and the `C` input buffers are
  zeroed with `std.crypto.secureZero` on every exit path of the module's own functions;
  `Tree.deinit` and `SecretKey.deinit` wipe the seeds; `Tree.init` and `Tree.sign` scrub
  16 KiB of stack below themselves (`xmss`'s measured `burnStack` trick). **Unverified:**
  there is no dead-stack residue test here (unlike `xmss`), so that scrub is by analogy;
  `SecretKey.init` takes the seed by value, and the caller's copy and any register/spill
  copies are outside the module (CONVENTIONS §2.1's caveat).
- **No internal RNG:** SEED (secret, uniformly random, used for nothing else, at least 32
  bytes — RFC 8554 §5.2) and `I` (16 bytes, random, RFC §7.1) are the caller's.
- **Allocation:** `Tree.init` / `SecretKey.init` / `sign` (when it builds a lower tree)
  allocate the public node cache and the cached certificates; both are public data and
  freed without wiping. `verify` never allocates.
- **`OutOfMemory` while building a tree burns no leaf** (the trees are built before the
  position moves); a hook error likewise. A process killed after the hook returned and
  before the signature was delivered wastes that leaf — the safe direction.
- **Unsupported typecodes** (0, the SHA-256/192 and SHAKE sets, anything unassigned) are
  `UnsupportedLmsType` / `UnsupportedOtsType` at parse and `false` at verify, never a
  guessed layout.

## Backlog / deferred

- **SHA-256/192 and SHAKE256 parameter sets (NIST SP 800-208; the later additional-sets RFC
  named in the task brief, not fetched here)** *(survey 2026-09-30)*. hbs-lms-rust and
  cisco/hash-sigs offer sets beyond the RFC 8554 SHA-256/256 ones *(inferred)*; a policy
  that mandates 192-bit or SHAKE cannot use this module. Moderate: `n`, `m` and the hash
  are module constants (`params.zig`, `core.zig`) and would become parameters; needs the
  new sets' KATs from the standard, not from an implementation. Pure Zig.
- **Faster HSS restart and signing state** *(survey 2026-09-30)*. Every restart rebuilds
  the top tree (`2^h0` leaves) and, on the first signature, the current lower trees. A
  documented serialisation of the node caches, or of the BDS-style traversal state
  `xmss` keeps, would make a restart cheap; it conflicts with the no-serialisation choice
  (a stale cache is not a secret, but a stale *position* is the hazard), so it is a decision
  for the maintainer. Also lower-tree pre-generation in a second thread so the boundary
  signature is not `O(2^h)`. Pure Zig.
- **Parallel and hardware-hash key generation** *(survey 2026-09-30)*. cisco/hash-sigs
  threads key generation *(inferred)*; here H20 takes hours. Splitting `subtreeRoot` per
  worker is straightforward (each height-`c` subtree is independent) and `std.Io` group
  primitives fit; SHA-NI use is already up to `std.crypto`. Moderate.
- **Verification-only build / `no_std` footprint** *(survey 2026-09-30)*. A device that only
  verifies still links the signing code unless the linker drops it; a `verify`-only entry
  point with a documented stack bound (`p * 32` is never held: the chain state is one
  `n`-byte value) is a small follow-up.
- **A foreign black-box oracle** (a differential run against cisco/hash-sigs's built binary
  through the wire format, not its source) and a **mutation run**, neither done for this
  first version; and a dead-stack residue test like `xmss`'s.
- **W1/W2 external vectors:** the RFC has none; a foreign implementation's output (as
  oracle) would give them.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class B · oracle MIXED

- **Class B** — published cryptographic construction with published vectors.
- **Oracle MIXED** — external for the paths the RFC's vectors reach, self for the rest;
  the evidence below names which.

**What the tests actually contain.** External (RFC 8554 Appendix F): verification of both
HSS signatures, regeneration of Test Case 2's two public keys from its SEED/I, and
byte-exact reproduction of both of its LMS signatures — LM-OTS W4 and W8, LMS H5 and H10,
HSS L = 2. Self (round trip, differential, recursive definition): W1 and W2, H15-H25, HSS
L = 3..8, mixed sets, the stateful discipline, the cache heights.

**How it got there.** RFC text only; the vectors were extracted by script from the RFC
and the hex sizes asserted against the format. No foreign implementation was run.
